title: Supreme Court: A UK Divorce Decree on 'Irretrievable Breakdown' Does Not Shield a Husband From Bigamy
case_name: A v. State of Andhra Pradesh through Secretary & Others (parties anonymised in reporting)
citation: 2026 INSC 1191, Criminal Appeal Nos. 5187-5189 of 2026, decided 3 November 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court held on 3 November 2026 that a UK decree dissolving a marriage for irretrievable breakdown, a ground the Hindu Marriage Act does not recognise, is not binding in India under Section 13 CPC. It sustained the bigamy complaint against the husband, who remarried in the UK after taking British citizenship, but quashed the case against his parents and second wife for want of proof they arranged it.
card_tip: An NRI who divorces abroad on a ground Indian matrimonial law does not recognise, then remarries, can still face a bigamy complaint in India because the first marriage is not legally dissolved here.
verification_notes: The citation 2026 INSC 1191, the 3 November 2026 decision date, the bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar, and the outcome (bigamy complaint sustained against the husband, quashed against his parents and second wife) are corroborated across the LiveLaw, Verdictum and Telangana Today (PTI) reports seen in this run. Sources differ on the exact style of cause, with Verdictum anonymising the appellant as 'A' and the State of Andhra Pradesh as respondent, which is used here as the more consistent form; one other source named the appellant but could not be independently cross-checked against the judgment, so that name is omitted. The judgment text itself was not opened in this run.
